claim: Long-term potentiation is a persistent strengthening of synaptic connections that underlies learning and memory formation
The prefrontal cortex is responsible for executive functions including planning decision-making and impulse control
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for interpret and recall information that confirms pre-existing beliefs
Flow state is a mental state of complete absorption in an activity characterized by focused attention and intrinsic motivation
Attachment theory describes how early bonds between children and caregivers shape emotional development and future relationships
The bystander effect describes how individuals are less likely to help in an emergency when other people are present
Cognitive load theory explains how working memory limitations affect learning and should inform instructional design
Growth mindset is the belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning leading to greater resilience
Interleaving practice mixing different problem types during study improves long-term retention compared to blocking by topic
Elaborative interrogation asking why and how questions while studying strengthens understanding and memory
The testing effect demonstrates that retrieving information from memory strengthens it more than additional study time
Dual process theory distinguishes between fast intuitive System 1 thinking and slow deliberative System 2 thinking
Neurogenesis the formation of new neurons occurs in the adult hippocampus and is influenced by exercise and learning
Mindfulness meditation has been shown to reduce symptoms of anxiety depression and chronic pain in clinical studies
The spacing effect shows that distributed practice over time produces better long-term retention than concentrated study sessions
Emotional intelligence includes the ability to perceive understand manage and use emotions in oneself and others
Scaffolding in education provides temporary structured support that is gradually removed as the learner develops competence
The Mozart effect the claim that listening to Mozart improves intelligence has been largely debunked by subsequent research
Post-traumatic growth describes positive psychological change experienced as a result of struggling with highly challenging life crises
Executive function develops throughout childhood and adolescence with the prefrontal cortex not fully maturing until the mid-twenties
